title: Kane wins Ballon d'Or, Putellas wins for third time
title_zh: 凯恩首夺金球奖，普特利亚斯第三次获奖

image.credit: Photo by Rob Griffin on Unsplash
image.author: Rob Griffin

lead: Harry Kane is the best football player of 2026. He won the men's Ballon d'Or in London. Alexia Putellas won the women's award.
lead_zh: 哈里·凯恩是2026年最佳足球运动员。他在伦敦获得了男子金球奖。阿莱克西娅·普特利亚斯获得了女子金球奖。
preview: Kane plays for Bayern Munich and England. He scored 77 goals in 68 games. He is the first Englishman to win in 25 years.
preview_zh: 凯恩效力于拜仁慕尼黑和英格兰队。他在68场比赛中打进了77个球。他是25年来第一位获此奖项的英格兰人。
paragraphs: Kane plays for Bayern Munich and England. He scored 77 goals in 68 games. He is the first Englishman to win in 25 years.
Putellas plays for Barcelona and Spain. This is her third Ballon d'Or. She won the award before, in 2021 and 2022.
Many other players won awards too. Lamine Yamal won the young player award for the third time. Bukayo Saka won the Socrates award for his charity.
paragraphs_zh: 凯恩效力于拜仁慕尼黑和英格兰队。他在68场比赛中打进了77个球。他是25年来第一位获此奖项的英格兰人。
普特利亚斯效力于巴塞罗那和西班牙队。这是她第三次获得金球奖。她曾在2021年和2022年获奖。
许多其他球员也获得了奖项。拉明·亚马尔第三次获得最佳年轻球员奖。布卡约·萨卡因其慈善事业获得了苏格拉底奖。
body:
Kane plays for Bayern Munich and England. He scored 77 goals in 68 games. He is the first Englishman to win in 25 years.

Putellas plays for Barcelona and Spain. This is her third Ballon d'Or. She won the award before, in 2021 and 2022.

Many other players won awards too. Lamine Yamal won the young player award for the third time. Bukayo Saka won the Socrates award for his charity.
body_zh:
凯恩效力于拜仁慕尼黑和英格兰队。他在68场比赛中打进了77个球。他是25年来第一位获此奖项的英格兰人。

普特利亚斯效力于巴塞罗那和西班牙队。这是她第三次获得金球奖。她曾在2021年和2022年获奖。

许多其他球员也获得了奖项。拉明·亚马尔第三次获得最佳年轻球员奖。布卡约·萨卡因其慈善事业获得了苏格拉底奖。

title_original: Ballon d’Or 2026: Harry Kane crowned in London ceremony as Putellas wins award for third time – as it happened
summary_original:
Alexia Putellas won the women’s Ballon d’Or for the third time while Harry Kane took the men’s, the first Englishman so to do for 25 years
Talking of UK winners,
it’s absolutely insane to think that, in 1968, three winners – Denis Law, Bobby Charlton and George Best – played in the same Manchester United team. Now, though, despite the money in the Premier League and with the exception of Erling Haaland and Bruno Fernandes, the best attackers are found in La Liga and Ligue 1. That looks likely to change only in the next generation and only if English clubs develop their own elite talent
DAZN have just interviewed Michael Owen, since the sad death of Kevin Keegan the only surviving British winner.
If I’m honest, he did pretty well to get that, which isn’t to decry his efforts – in Rome and Cardiff especially – but the best player in the world? Not for me, Clive.
Continue reading...

Righto, Barney Ronay’s match report is here…
…which means that’s it from me. Thanks all for your company and comments – sorry I couldn’t get to them all – mazal tov to all the winners, Alexia and Aitch in particular, and peace out.
23m ago
19.23 EDT
I’ve no clue how he managed all that without leaking eyeballs; I’m halfway there myself.
I guess that’s the kind of composure that gets you 77 goals in 68 appearances, an absolute outrage of a season.
27m ago
19.20 EDT
“And then lastly for me it’s just the journey.
For any young boy or girl wanting to achieve their dream, anything is possible with hard work when no one else is watching. To go through the ups and downs, to learn with resilience, determination and self-belief … anything is possible.
My journey wasn’t straightforward, I wasn’t the kid who went straight to the top. I had to experience the downs, I had to experience a lot of low moves, I had to fight my way to be the very best right now and i hope that can give you inspiration. Thank you.”
Well said, Aitch/Haitch; beautifully done.
31m ago
19.16 EDT
Now he moves to Kate, his wife and best friend. They’ve been through ups and downs; she’s his biggest supporter and wanted this more than he did.
There was an anxious wait to find out, “it’s been horrible for you so here it is, we dun it. Yo always want the best for me, you sacrifice yourself to help me achieve my dreams and I know they’re your dreams as well. It wouldn’t be possible without you, this is trophy that we celebrate, me and you, all our close-knit team so I just want to say i love and celebrate tonight, I love you.”
34m ago
19.13 EDT
Finally it’s his kids, past whose bedtime it is; goodness me, imagine Harry Kane being your dad, and yet at the same time, it won’t matter, he’s just their dad.
They’re the reason he does this, they might not appreciate it yet and he brings a few trophies home, but this one’s a special one.
“I can’t wait to see you and celebrate with you, I want to set a good example, being a father but also being a professional, what it means to work hard, what it means to believe in yourself and yeah, I love you very much.” Gosh, he’s giving out a lot of love here and it’s moving to enjoy.
37m ago
19.09 EDT
Now it’s on to his parents, who’ve travelled all over watching him play without ever putting pressure on him to become a footballer –
“It was always about working hard, it was always about improving, it was always about learning,”, a lesson there for us all. The traits they’ve given him have allowed him to be successful, and he loves them. Ahhh, that’s a lovely tribute, may we all cause our kids to feel that way about us.
40m ago
19.07 EDT
His brother-agent Charlie is next
– “It doesn’t seem like long ago since we were kicking a ball about in the garden and park, watching football, talking about football, just football mad – “and looking like Scott Dissick,” he neglects to add.
He knows Charlie says he gave him his ability, so thanks him for that, and to have an older brother like that, who travels around the world to watch him, giving up time with his family to support.
43m ago
19.04 EDT
Now it’s on to the personal thanks, starting with Dr Alejandro Iloriago Callapo, with whom he’s been working for seven years – since he tore his hamstring pretty much off the bone.
He thanks the work that no one sees, giving up time away from family, and the friendship they’ve formed, is a true honour.
Now it’s on to Kelly, Gary and Tom, his parents and brother-in-law. They live their emotions together, they’ve made him feel part of the family since he stepped into their house at 18 and they allow him to do what he does on the pitch through what they do off it.
46m ago
19.00 EDT
“Wow, wow wow” begins our Ballon d’Or laurearte, saying it’s lucky he’s got a list.
He thanks France Football, all those who voted for him, it was a difficult choice, and his teammates, some of whom he was up against.
He then talks about how his teammates push him, citing Dayot Upamecano, who he faces in training, then sends his best wishes to Vincent Kompany, hoping this has given him a lift.
He moves on to the Bayern suits, musing on what an honour it is to play for the club, then he talks about England, saying it wasn’t exactly what they wanted, but they had a great year, it’s an honour to captain the squad, and Thomas Tuchel also pushed him.
Now it’s on to Spurs, cue wild cheers in the auditorium. He wouldn’t be where he is today without the club, he was there from 11, living his dream, and he thanks the Spurs fans around the world. The support he gets in the ground, on social media – he appreciates it all. He used to be a fan himself and anytime he can give back he’s happy to.
Now it’s on to coaches who’ve helped him –Bradley Allen, Chris Ramsey, John McDermott, Alex Inglethopre, Ryan Mason, who’s one of his best friends, Kenny Jackett, Russell Slade, Mauricio Pochettino, Tim Sherwood, Jose Mourinho Antonio Conte, Roy Hodgson, Garethg Southgate, then Vinny and Thomas all of whom played a key role in his development and without any of them he wouldn’t be here now.
